rv.q: Decouflé’s choreography is unsurpassable in its elastic grace and athleticism without seeming circus-like.
It’s an entertaining and audacious endeavour – the book is better, but there’s room for both.

The difficulty is that, as beguiling as this production sometimes is, the more profound questions it’s asking about love and identity are often lost beneath – or overwhelmed by – the sheer busyness of its whirling walls, video projections and dancing waiters.
Decouflé's production retains the absurdist tropes but will leave you none the wiser about what Murakami has to say about human consciousness and the struggle to truly know ourselves.

So what a delight to be able to report that Philippe Decouflé’s production is an exquisite dramatisation of the novel, filled with stunningly sculpted stage pictures, haunting music, and elegant choreography.
Visually and choreographically, the production is an absolute triumph.
This adaptation (almost three hours long) drifts when it could punch and delights in its own existence, almost to the exclusion of us on the other side of the fourth wall.
The result is a sensory spectacle that feels perfectly Murakami: dreamlike, dazzling and totally different to anything you’ve seen before.
This is a production that looks beautiful and has a certain magic about it, combining imaginative stagecraft, inventive choreography and powerful storytelling in a way that feels genuinely original.
Every moment of End of the World and Hard-Boiled Wonderland is imbued with a profound sense of wonder and solitude.
Yet, for all its shortcomings, the production is undeniably pleasant to watch — and that is no small achievement.
Ultimately, this lush, atmospheric new Murakami adaptation honours the singular strangeness and narrative lumpiness of its source material in equal measure.

cn.t: Visually stunning but narratively tangled adaptation of Murakami's novel dazzles with inventive choreography and dreamlike imagery, though critics split on whether the spectacle compensates for a confusing, overly sanitized story that struggles to capture the source material's to
